content: Integration tests run against real Postgres via Testcontainers — never H2. H2 hides Postgres-specific bugs (type mapping, casing) and cannot honestly exercise the partial-eval -> SQL feature. The build auto-discovers a podman socket (podman machine inspect) and disables Ryuk; explicit DOCKER_HOST wins; CI provides Docker.

Clean-room rule for every review: no proprietary names, identifiers, comments, or copied text may land in committed files. Anything informed by prior proprietary work must be an original reimplementation. opa-abac-core must have zero Spring dependency. Reject diffs that violate either.

name: Suspect the OPA/auth layer first when E2E stalls in 403 loops
description: When integration/E2E flows stall in a 'call -> 403 -> retry' loop on resources just created, suspect OPA/gateway returning deny before suspecting the app. Two quick checks: (1) replay the call with a fresh token through the gateway — if it 403s, it's auth; (2) bypass the gateway straight to the app with the same token — if it 200s, the auth layer is the problem. Collection-level endpoints often work while per-item endpoints 403 because the per-item path needs a policy/data lookup that's failing (stale policy, downed PIP).

content: Prompt-craft for the autonomous-implementation prompt (from Jaymin West's Agentic Engineering Book, Prompt chapter; folded into docs/guides/AUTONOMOUS-IMPLEMENTATION-FLOW.md §7.0 + §8): (1) PINK-ELEPHANT — negative 'NEVER do X' constraints backfire in long contexts (InstructGPT/16x.engineer): naming the forbidden action activates it, so the agent drifts toward it over a long run. Prefer positive reframes ('core stays Spring-free' > 'NEVER import Spring'; 'residual AND-ed with scope' > 'never replace scope'). Reserve hard NEVER only for unrecoverable boundaries (do-NOT-push, clean-room). (2) Critical constraints FIRST — model weights earlier content. (3) DECLARATIVE goals / IMPERATIVE steps (~23% reasoning gain, SatLM arxiv:2305.09656): frame 'The problem' + fail-closed invariant as a target STATE, keep the per-ticket loop as imperative steps. (4) Specificity where there's an objective right answer (output/format/boundary/the exact test that proves a ticket), flexibility on implementation approach; give core principles + 1 canonical example, not 47 edge cases. (5) MATURITY MODEL: autonomous prompt ~L4 contextual, deep-review ~L5 composed, slice-planner ~L6 template-metaprompt; the L6 principle 'separate Expertise from Workflow, only Expertise updates' maps onto our split — stable prompt skeleton (Workflow) + growing Mulch (Expertise). The autonomous run IS the long-context scenario these findings target.

name: Periodic whole-repo adversarial review catches cross-slice seams
description: First full-repo review (post-Phase-5.9): 4-lens parallel fan-out (core+starter / security+data adversarial fail-closed audit / examples+rego+infra / docs accuracy), synthesis spot-verifies every High-Medium finding in source before acceptance. All four Medium fail-open seams (interface-annotation pointcut dodge, null-resourceId widening, subtree-outlives-OPA-outage, kill-switch drops deny filter) came from the adversarial fail-closed lens told to enumerate error paths and find an open one — and each was invisible to per-slice review because it lives at a boundary BETWEEN slices. Keep: run a whole-repo adversarial pass every few slices; per-slice gates do not cover seams. Also: docs lens must diff README against implemented/ folders — the front door goes stale fastest.

name: Audit skills ported: doc-audit + e2e-audit (incremental manifest model)
description: Ported 2026-06-11 from the private portal instantiation (clean-room rewrite, token-frugal redesign). Both are local gitignored skills wrapping a workflow: .claude/skills/doc-audit/ (living docs vs current code; ~35-doc corpus — excludes docs/to-do/implemented, frozen history) and .claude/skills/e2e-audit/ (7 postman collections vs the repo e2e conventions incl. the fixture-id registry). MODEL: the report frontmatter IS the manifest — rubricVersion + per-item git hash-object sha; the SKILL does all bookkeeping deterministically in main context (no scope agent): changed-set only, carry-forward verdicts, auto-changelog, 'nothing changed -> say so and STOP' zero-cost path; reports -> docs/audits/ on a docs/*-audit-<date> branch, clean-room-scanned (blocklist from scripts/planning/cleanroom-patterns.local), never pushed. GOTCHA FIXED: Workflow args can arrive as a JSON-encoded STRING (portal tolerates the '(undated)' symptom); both workflows now parse either form — without this the doc list silently came up empty. PROMPT RULE: auditors must cite repo-RELATIVE paths (smoke run cited absolute /Users/... paths; the clean-room gate would trip on them). COST PROFILE (smoke, 2026-06-11): ~48k subagent tokens per doc audited; e2e registry-only sweep = 1 agent / ~49k. Full 35-doc baseline ~1.7M subagent tokens -> run it in ~3 batches via the maxDocs=12 cap (overflow defers). Lows skip the skeptic by design (unverified:true in the payload). Smoke found real drift: TAG-SYSTEM vocabulary (4 undocumented area/ tags, status/implemented on 7 LIBRARY-SPINE notes, an audience/ namespace) and ADR 0011 §4 illustrative error codes that don't exist as shipped (TAG_KEY_UNKNOWN -> actual TAG_VALUE_ILLEGAL; STATE_CONFLICT -> ROLE_IMMUTABLE / TEAM_TARGET_EXISTS).

name: Empty adversarial-review result: spot-verify by hand; the dead-code lens cannot see outside the diff
description: Second run of the multi-lens adversarial review workflow (5.95 pagination slice, 7 lenses + refutation): ZERO confirmed findings. Two process lessons. (1) An empty result is a claim, not a proof — the reviewer still hand-traces the load-bearing items in main context (fail-closed branches each mapped to a proving test; additivity via 'pre-existing tests green unmodified'; authorization byte-identity via annotation-line diffs == 0; an overflow spot-check on new index math). On 5.95 the hand pass CONFIRMED the empty result — the per-ticket review gates (which had already caught a composition duplication, an orphaned method, and a wrong exception type mid-run) had pre-drained the findings pool; a clean adversarial pass over a gate-disciplined autonomous run is a plausible outcome, not automatically a tooling failure. (2) Diff-scoped lenses are blind to dead code in UNTOUCHED files — carry such items into the review via the run's STATUS notes (STATUS-03 flagged two caller-less CategoryRepository derived queries; the review verified zero callers repo-wide and deleted them). QA verdict for the autonomous-runs retrospective: the 5.95 run's own gates missed nothing the deep review found — no laziness signal.

name: Invariant-shaped rules; refutation narrows, the critic widens; sweep siblings
description: META-LESSONS adopted 2026-06-12 from a root-cause audit of the source platform's review stack (strong implementer + multi-gate review still shipped race/recovery defects). (1) WRITE INVARIANTS, NOT MECHANISMS: a rule phrased as one incident's mechanical fix ('lock first', 're-fetch fresh in the tx') is satisfied literally by defective code — code can lock first and still act on decisions made on unlocked state. State the generating invariant (CONCURRENCY-AND-LOCKING Rules 1-2: decide under the protection you act under; bind decision version to acted-on version) and keep mechanisms as named instances. (2) REFUTE-ONLY PIPELINES ONLY SHRINK: adversarial verification cannot add the unswept-sibling / zero-caller-seam / untested-off-state findings no lens generated — the deep-review workflow now has a Critic phase that widens (its candidates face the same refutation). (3) SIBLING SWEEP: a review fix in handler X is grepped across X's mirrored siblings (same base class / mirrored operation / the other example service) and fixed in the same commit. (4) HAPPY-PATH FRAMING EXCLUDES RECOVERY EDGES: decomposition acceptance must exercise a non-happy path through every new seam (SPI, property, guard, advice, accessor, rego entrypoint, recovery edge) — zero callers = not done. (5) SECURITY + CONCURRENCY/IDEMPOTENCY are first-class review lenses on every non-docs diff (maintainer priority), not subsets of fail-closed.

name: Whole-tree retro-audit validates the always-on lenses
description: Retro-audit shape: surface-partitioned fan-out (not diff-shaped), two always-on lenses, adversarial refutation, critic; report RETRO-AUDIT-2026-06-12.md; fixes f453e12.

name: The completeness critic earns its keep: it found the 6.7 unswept drift-guard the run's own gates + e2e missed
description: 6.7 deep-review (multi-lens adversarial, 8 lenses, 12 agents): 0 fail-open/widening/concurrency defects survived refutation — the slice was clean on the dimensions that matter most. The TWO findings both came from the COMPLETENESS CRITIC, not the lenses: (1 Medium) the CI drift guard + U9 parity didn't cover the two NEW service-bundle mirror files a slice added (an unswept sibling of the guard); (2 Low) a stale team:manage javadoc in the pinned-untouched MembershipService (an unswept sibling of the controller verb-rename). Neither is a defect a refutation-only pipeline could surface — no lens generated them, so there was nothing to refute; they are missing-wiring/unswept-sibling findings the critic is specifically designed to WIDEN into (per mx-27b7c7 'refutation narrows, the critic widens'). Signal for the autonomous-runs retro QA line: the run's own ★ gates verified byte-identity ad-hoc (diff) but did not ADD an enforced guard for the files it newly mirrored — a laziness-adjacent gap (consequence-not-swept), caught only post-run. Lesson: keep the completeness critic on for any slice that GROWS a mirrored set / adds a seam; the always-on lenses confirm the happy path is safe, the critic finds the consequence the diff didn't sweep.

name: Autonomous-run self-corrections don't self-propagate: sibling-sweep the CLAIM (esp. runbooks); STATUS 'e2e proves X' needs cell-level audit (shape vs cut); the critic finds unreachable-but-untested paths
description: ACTION-ENRICHMENT deep-review (multi-lens adversarial, 8 lenses + refutation + completeness critic, 20 agents): 0 fail-open/widening/security/concurrency/core-boundary/rego-decision defects — the load-bearing invariants held. All 10 confirmed findings (0 refuted) were documentation-accuracy or test-coverage honesty. TWO meta-lessons the review surfaced, both about an AUTONOMOUS RUN'S OWN SELF-CORRECTIONS: (1) SELF-CORRECTION DOESN'T SELF-PROPAGATE. Mid-run the author discovered "zero Rego change" was false (Phase 5 had added bulk only to category.rego), corrected ADR 0016 §6 — but left the SAME falsehood in 5 sibling docs (the matrix run-script header, scripts/postman/README row, E2E-TESTING x2, the slice 10-QA doc) + 4 design-statement echoes (00-DESIGN, 01-DECOMPOSITION, the autonomous prompt). The Critical was the operationally-misleading runbook line: it tells an operator "no OPA restart", but OPA has no --watch and the new bulk rule must load, so following it makes catalog/product enrichment silently degrade (all-false -> _actions omitted -> the e2e cell fails). LESSON: when a fix corrects a CLAIM that was repeated across docs/runbooks, sibling-sweep the CLAIM the same way you'd sweep a code defect — grep the exact phrase repo-wide; a correction that lands in one doc but not its echoes is a half-fix, and the surviving echo in a RUNBOOK actively breaks the operator. (2) SELF-PREFERENTIAL BIAS IN STATUS NOTES. STATUS-06 claimed the live e2e 'proved everything', but the populated-team _actions path had no test (getTeam is ungated -> always the absent-degrade; TeamEnrichable + the team bulk rule had zero positive coverage) and the E4 'omit-on-failure live' cell asserted vacuously (paused OPA also 403s the gate, so it never exercised a gate-allowed read whose enrichment fails). The completeness critic (not the refuters) found the unreachable-but-untested team path — refutation can only narrow, the critic widens. LESSON: a 'the e2e proves X' status claim must be checked against what the cells ACTUALLY assert (shape vs the cut); an e2e cell that depends on a shared dependency (OPA) being down cannot isolate one consumer's failure — relabel it a smoke check and point at the unit/IT that controls gate and dependency independently.

name: A defect-CLASS fix must sweep the class repo-wide inside the run; the critic keeps catching the cross-service sibling
description: Third instance of the completeness critic finding what refutation structurally cannot (after mx-98fc1a, mx-3959dc): the DIRECTORY-QUERY-FILTERS run's T3 fixed the 406-on-bare-JSON-Accept class for ALL FOUR 204-only ops in the user-mgmt spec — and never looked at the OTHER example service, whose three mirrored DELETE ops (deleteCatalog/deleteCategory/deleteProduct) had the identical latent 406. The run's ★ gate checked additivity/wiring within the ticket's service; ticket scoping ('same service' in the decomposition) quietly bounded the sweep. Rule: when a ticket fixes a NAMED DEFECT CLASS (not an instance), the run itself greps the whole repo for the class signature (here: any '204' response with no success content in any openapi/*.yaml) before declaring the ticket done — do not leave the cross-service mirror to the deep-review. The deep-review sibling sweep remains the backstop, not the owner.

name: The sibling sweep includes TEST CELLS: a handler adopting a mirrored dispatch must inherit the mirror's test cells
description: Deep-review of PR #65 (2026-07-10): the catalog PUT adopted the category's delta dispatch VERBATIM (TagDecisionGate), and the code sweep was done — but every dispatch TEST cell (I13-I16) still targeted only the category endpoint, so the catalog's tags-delta / both-in-order / denied-assign-tags / create-with-tags paths shipped with zero coverage. Two of the five review findings were exactly this class (the critic lens caught them; the code-focused lenses did not). RULE: when handler X adopts handler Y's pattern, the sweep checklist is code + SPEC (the OpenAPI 422/503 declarations were also missing, on X AND pre-existing on Y's update op) + TEST CELLS (mirror Y's cells onto X in the same commit) + E2E (a new gateway-observable cut gets a newman cell — the ADR-0022 exemption had only rego tests until 6a/6b). Related: run the FULL local suite before push, not targeted ITs — the I6 verb-set pin escaped to CI that way in the same PR.
